title: feat(types): `ObjectChartSchema` accepts the react tier's `object-chart` node — the spec's `{ name }` series arm, family as `specType` (objectui#10770)
body:
Fixes #10770
Clause-②: yes

## What this does

The react tier's `ObjectChart` block authors `@objectstack/spec`'s `ChartConfigSchema`. Its react-blocks entry has `schemaType: 'object-chart'` and `schema: ChartConfigSchema`, and lists `type` and `series` in its data props. The react-page wrapper turns the objectstack showcase `renewals-pipeline` page's block into an `object-chart` node shaped `{ specType: 'bar', series: [{ name: 'total', label: 'Invoice value' }], … }`. It parks the author's `type` as `specType` because `type` is the node's discriminator. Both faces of `ObjectChartSchema` refused that node.

This aligns the contract face with the spec (ruling `5617465269` principle 1, objectui#7759):

- **`series` element: two arms.** An entry is either the spec's `ChartSeriesSchema` (TS: `ChartSeries`), BY REFERENCE, which is the AUTHOR arm, or the unchanged INTERNAL `{ dataKey }` arm that the relays compose.
- **`specType` is declared**, as the spec's `ChartTypeSchema` (TS: `ChartType`), by reference.
- **`chartType` is optional.** A zod `.superRefine` (`requireObjectChartFamily`) requires one of `chartType` or `specType`. That is the floor the required flag used to carry, so a node that names no family is still refused, at `chartType`. The TS interface cannot say "one of two"; the docblock states this as a ceiling.
- **Docblocks.** The `series` verdict ("INTERNAL … All five producers compose it") is rewritten: the react-page wrapper is a sixth producer, and it forwards the authored array untouched.

⛔ There is no objectui-only dialect: both new crossings are spec symbols, bound by reference. ⛔ There is no renderer change: `normalizeChartSchema` already reads `specType` and translates the `{ name }` arm (one-time probe below). No other schema was changed.

## Step 1: does any door run this schema on the wrapper's node? No.

- **Render.** `SchemaRenderer` runs core's structural `validateSchema` (development only), not zod. The react-page wrapper runs no zod.
- **Publish.** objectstack's react-page gate (`packages/lint/src/validate-react-page-props.ts`, read at objectstack `fdb2669`) reads the block's binding VALUES and resolves `series[].dataKey ?? series[].name`; the only schemas it parses are `ChartAggregateSchema` and `ChartDrillDownSchema`. objectstack imports no `@object-ui/types`: every hit in its tree is prose.
- **`objectui validate`.** It parses one JSON or YAML document. A react page's `source` is an opaque string: `safeValidateSchema` of a `{ type: 'page', kind: 'react', source }` document carrying this block PASSES and never judges the block.
- **Other runtime importers.** Outside the types package, `@object-ui/types/zod` is imported at runtime only by the CLI (`validate`, `check`) and by plugin-map (`ObjectMapConfigSchema`).

⇒ No user met the refusal. The defect was on the contract face, and in the docblock's INTERNAL-only claim. This reading gives no reason to raise the grade.

**Before** (unmodified face, a probe on the wrapper-built node): `ObjectChartSchema.safeParse` gives `invalid_value` at `chartType` and `invalid_type` at `series.0.dataKey`; `safeValidateSchema` gives the same two. **After**: it parses with zero issues on both.

## Files

In the claim's file surface:
- `packages/types/src/objectql.ts` and `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts`, within the `ObjectChartSchema` block and its spec imports.
- the new pin `packages/types/src/__tests__/object-chart-react-tier-node-10770.test.ts`. It pins that the showcase node parses (on the mirror and through `safeValidateSchema`), that a series entry with neither `name` nor `dataKey` and a node naming no family are refused, that the author arm is strict and `specType` takes every spec `ChartTypeSchema` value, and the TS twin.
- `.changeset/10770-object-chart-react-tier-node.md`: `@object-ui/types` **minor**.
- `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`: no row moved (green, unedited).

Beyond the claim's surface. Each is a pin that the widening falsified, not a drive-by:
- `packages/types/src/__tests__/widget-schema-anchors-7946.test.ts`: `assertionSeriesBindsDataKey` indexed `['dataKey']` on the element and went compile-red. It now reads the internal arm through `Extract`.
- `packages/types/src/__tests__/imported-defaults-8317.test.ts`: its census failed by name ("a schema imported by a mirror is not in this file's `IMPORTED` list … Add it", naming `ChartSeriesSchema`). The schema was added to the list.
- `packages/plugin-charts/src/__tests__/ObjectChart.schemaAnchor-7946.test.ts`: a consumer pin asserting the OPPOSITE (a `@ts-expect-error` that `series: [{ name: 'amount' }]` is refused). It went "Unused @ts-expect-error" once the rebuilt `dist` carried the union, which also serves as the reverse proof that the consumer compiled against the new declaration. It now pins the refusal that stands (`[{ label: 'amount' }]`). PR objectui#10787 does not touch this file (its file list was read).

## Patch round 1 (final head `77646f4150`)

The first CI run's required `Spec Main Shape Gate` was **cancelled** at its 45-minute timeout in step 12, the whole-tree type-check. The patch round measured the cause, and it was a **degraded runner, not this PR**:
- **The whole-tree type-check** (the gate's step-12 command, forced) takes the same time with and without this PR:
  - pinned: 472 s vs 480 s at the merge base;
  - spec `main` `17bd318`: 485 s vs 488 s;
  - the objectstack commit the failed job compiled (`e462186`): 490 s, 81/81 tasks.

  The types program gains +0.2% instantiations, with no hot `ObjectChartSchema` construct in a `--generateTrace`.
- **The failed job was slow on every step**, including steps that never read this diff: spec build 547 s vs 109–156 s on four neighbouring gate jobs, and pack 62 s vs 10–13 s.
- **No source changed.** The only commit is a merge of `origin/main` `12809a595a`. At `77646f4150` the gate is green in 12.1 min, and every CI job is green (`Type Check` 7.1 min). The seat's earlier diagnosis on this PR was corrected at `5858943102`.

## Acceptance notes

- **Mixed entry.** An entry that writes both `name` and `dataKey` parses through the internal arm with `name` stripped. That is the internal arm's existing strip posture, unchanged; the renderer reads `dataKey` first, so the drawn column is the same.
- **Both family keys on one node.** A node writing both `chartType` and `specType` is accepted, and `normalizeChartSchema` takes `chartType` first. It is not refused here, because that would be a new rule.
- **`specType` value domain.** `specType` accepts all of the spec's `ChartTypeSchema` values. `normalizeChartSchema` leaves a family it does not draw (`metric`, `table`, …) unset, which is already pinned by `normalizeChartSchema.test.ts` ("leaves a family this renderer cannot draw unset"). This is a pre-existing seam between spec and renderer. Carrier: none; noted, not filed.
- **Publish-gate leniency.** objectstack's react-page gate resolves `series[].dataKey` and `xAxisKey` on this block as legitimate, while the spec's `ChartSeriesSchema` refuses `dataKey` by name. That is leniency in objectstack's lint; it is not measured through `os validate` here. Carrier: none; noted, not filed.
- **Comparison guard.** `ObjectChart`'s `chartTypeIgnoresCompareTo(schema.chartType)` reads `chartType` only, not `specType`. `compareTo` is not a react-block prop, so this is dormant. Carrier: none; noted, not filed.
- **Instrument drift under main's zod.** Under zod@4.6.1, which main's spec resolves, `imported-defaults-8317.test.ts`'s "no member became REQUIRED" goes red for 16 schemas, 15 of them pre-existing plus `ChartSeriesSchema`. zod 4.6.1 reports `_zod.optin === 'defaulted'` for a member with a default, while its stripped twin reads `'optional'`. Both are omissible, so this is instrument drift, not a narrowed accept set. It surfaces on the zod ^4.6.1 floor bump. Carrier: none (the next spec pin bump); noted, not filed.
- **Superseded pending changesets.** The pending changesets for objectui#10584, the objectui#7946 anchor and objectui#8086 describe `series` as the internal `{ dataKey }` arm only. They record their own PRs, and this changeset supersedes them in the same release, so they are not edited.
- **Card residue.** The residue named on the card, app-shell `ObjectView` forwarding `viewDef.chart.series` verbatim, is untouched.
